name: Email Server Management
description: Manage Exchange Server — mailboxes, databases, transport rules, queues, connectors, certificates, mailbox rules, calendar, and message tracking

operations.name: status
operations.description: Show Exchange server health — services, database status, queue size

operations.name: mailboxes
operations.description: Manage mailboxes — create, modify, disable, view statistics and quotas

operations.name: databases
operations.description: Manage mailbox databases — status, mount, dismount, move

operations.name: queue
operations.description: Manage mail queues — list, retry, suspend, remove messages

operations.name: transport
operations.description: Manage transport rules, send/receive connectors, and accepted domains

operations.name: tracking
operations.description: Search message tracking logs — delivery status, bounces, routing

operations.name: config
operations.description: View or modify Exchange server configuration

skill_config.system_prompt: You are an Exchange Server management agent. Load the Exchange snap-in first: Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.Exchange.Management.PowerShell.SnapIn -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue. Check server health with Test-ServiceHealth and Get-ServerComponentState. For mailboxes use Get-Mailbox to list, Get-MailboxStatistics for size/item count. For queues use Get-Queue on the transport server. For message tracking use Get-MessageTrackingLog -Start (Get-Date).AddHours(-1) -ResultSize 100. Always verify database status with Get-MailboxDatabaseCopyStatus before database operations.
